title: Contract witness: streaming-safe JSONSchema shim and OpenAI-compat error mapping
author: Linnea Chen
release_notes: Introduces an opt-in 'contract witness' mode that preserves streaming stability while deferring strict JSON Schema validation until stream completion. Adds OpenAI-compat error mapping for structured output failures and a per-request strictness toggle. No breaking behavior by default.
changed_files: runtime/response_contract/witness_buffer.go (new) - implements incremental capture of structured output tokens with checkpointing and size limits
runtime/response_contract/validator.go - deferred validator that runs after stream end and emits structured diagnostics
gateway/openai_compat/response_mapper.go - maps validator diagnostics to OpenAI-style error objects and codes
api/response_format/handler.go - adds support for ?response_format=contract_witness and header X-Redwood-Contract-Strict
sdk/python/redwood/structured_output.py - client-side opt-in helper and local precheck utilities
docs/api/response_format.md - documents witness mode, examples, and migration guidance
tests/e2e/contract_witness_toolcall.test - end-to-end test exercising streaming + tool calls + deferred validation

OpenAI mapping: translate validator diagnostics into compat error objects (linnea/openai-mapping)

body:
Motivation and summary:
We need a way to support strict JSON Schema enforcement for structured output without regressing streaming stability or tool/function calling semantics. Naive synchronous schema validation on streaming output can cause deadlocks, increase tail latency, and break tool-call handoffs when the model emits partial or out-of-order chunks.

This PR introduces an opt-in 'contract witness' mode which captures structured-output tokens incrementally during streaming, allows tool calls to interleave, and performs strict validation only once the stream completes (or once a terminal marker is observed). When validation fails, the runtime emits a well-structured diagnostic and — for OpenAI compatibility — maps the failure to familiar error objects/codes so existing integrations can detect and handle contract violations.

Key behaviors and guarantees:
- Default behavior unchanged: nothing is strict unless the request opts in via response_format=contract_witness or header X-Redwood-Contract-Strict: true.
- Streaming remains low-latency: witness buffer is bounded and write-paths are fast-pathed; validator runs off the critical path.
- Tool/function calls are preserved: tool call tokens are recorded and forwarded immediately; validation treats tool outputs as part of the assembled document at validation time.
- OpenAI-compat mapping: validator diagnostics are translated to a small set of error codes (contract_error, contract_malformed_output, contract_partial_stream) and an 'error_details' payload that mirrors OpenAI error object shapes to minimize integration work.

What changed (high level):
- witness_buffer.go: incremental ring-buffer with checkpoints. The buffer supports partial commit so very large outputs don't OOM; if the buffer limit is reached we fall back to a small streaming-coercion mode and mark validation as skipped with a clear diagnostic.
- validator.go: performs JSON Schema v4/v7 validation against the assembled payload, returns granular diagnostics, and includes a lightweight suggestion mechanism (e.g., 'missing property: tool_response').
- response_mapper.go: adds OpenAI-style error mapping so clients using the compat layer can rely on stable error shapes.
- API surface: implemented response_format=contract_witness and header toggle. Added flags to the request context so downstream pieces know whether to enforce strictness or not.
- SDK helpers: Python client gained a convenience to opt-in and to local pre-validate common schemas to catch errors earlier in dev cycles.
- Observability: added metrics for witness validation latency and failure counts; dashboards will be updated in a follow-up.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement witness buffer and deferred validator
- [x] Preserve tool/function-call delivery semantics during streaming
- [x] Add OpenAI-compat error mapping for diagnostics
- [x] Unit tests for validator and mapper
- [x] E2E test covering streaming + tool calls + validation failure path
- [x] Docs and migration guidance
- [x] Benchmarks showing <5% median latency regression for typical 1-2s streams

Testing notes and CI:
- CI ran the full unit and integration suite. One flaky e2e test (tests/e2e/stream_replay.test) failed on the first run; we re-ran and it passed. All checks are green now.
- Added tests to simulate: (1) valid structured output streaming, (2) invalid late-arriving token that breaks schema, (3) large outputs hitting witness buffer cap, (4) interleaved tool calls followed by a schema failure.

Reviewer convo (highlights):
- Connor Hayes: "We need to be explicit about memory caps and the UX when buffer limits hit — does the client get an error, or do we surface a partial-success?"
  - Linnea: "Implemented: when cap hits we emit a 'validation_skipped_due_to_buffer_limit' diagnostic and return a contract_partial_stream OpenAI-style error. Client still receives streamed tokens and tool calls as normal; the post-stream validation result will indicate partiality."

- Asha Patel: "Can we do a fast-path for tiny schemas (single-field objects)?"
  - Linnea: "Yes, added micro-optimizations in perf-tune commit. For schemas with <= 3 properties we do a lightweight incremental check during streaming (cheap heuristics only) to catch obvious problems early without blocking."

- Diego Morales: "Mapping to OpenAI errors looks good, but document the exact shapes for SDKs."
  - Linnea: "Added examples in docs/api/response_format.md and the Python helper provides an object wrapper to decode compat errors. Will add TS/Go in follow-ups."

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Large sustained streams could amplify memory usage. Mitigation: witness buffer cap with clear diagnostic; we also added an autoscaling knob on dedicated pools to better handle high-concurrency streaming workloads.
- Risk: Users relying on synchronous validation semantics may be surprised. Mitigation: opt-in only, docs and SDK helpers to surface the difference, and a migration guide.

Backward compatibility:
- No changes to default request behavior. The runtime only engages witness/strict behavior when explicitly requested by response_format or header. OpenAI-compat mapping only affects the compat layer surface for requests using structured output modes.

Follow-ups (planned):
- Add TS/Go SDK helpers to decode compat errors (ENG-4123)
- Dashboard update and runbook for validation failure patterns (ENG-4179)
- Telemetry sampling to escape noisy validation failures in large fleets (ENG-4204)

Merge notes:
- Squashed and merged after CI green and approvals from Connor and Asha. Diego provided an approving review after the mapping clarifications were addressed.

References:
- Linear: ENG-4122, ENG-4123
- Incident: SUP-1301 referenced a customer issue where synchronous validation caused timeouts during tool-calls

If you want to try it locally: add header 'X-Redwood-Contract-Strict: true' to a generation request or append '?response_format=contract_witness' and stream the output; the final response envelope will include 'contract_validation' when the witness mode is used.
notes: This PR aims for minimal default-surface change. Contract witness is opt-in and feature-flagged for staged rollout.
We validated performance on a medium traffic cluster; detailed dashboards coming in a follow-up PR.
